headline: Record sales, EBITDA and backlog; guidance raised again
summary_short: Nordson's Q2 FY2026 sales rose 8.5% y/y to a second-quarter record $740.8M on 7% organic growth, with EBITDA up 8.3% to $235.2M; GAAP EPS of $2.09 (+6.1% y/y) absorbed a $24.0M pension settlement charge, while adjusted EPS hit a record $2.86 (+18.2% y/y).
summary_long: Sales rose 8.5% y/y (7% organic, 3% FX) to a Q2 record $740.8M, with growth across all three segments. Gross margin held roughly flat at 54.5% (-20bp y/y). Operating profit rose 16.9% y/y to $197.2M as revenue growth outpaced flat SG&A. GAAP net income of $117.3M (+4.4% y/y, EPS $2.09) absorbed a $24.0M non-cash pension settlement charge and a loss on minority investments; adjusted EPS excluding these hit a record $2.86 (+18.2% y/y). Cash fell to $102.0M after $129.3M of buybacks and $91.6M of dividends YTD. Nordson raised full-year guidance to $2,930-3,010M sales and $11.30-11.80 adjusted EPS, and guided Q3 sales of $760-790M.

All KPI deltas in this summary were instead computed directly from the primary document's own consolidated income statement and segment tables (three-months and six-months columns), which are internally consistent and tie out exactly (e.g. six-month net income $250,698 minus Q2 $117,316 = $133,382, matching the release's own Jan-31-YTD column). drivers.explanation: Organic sales increased 7% driven by growth in all three segments, plus 3% favorable currency translation, partly offset by the previously announced divestiture and a small precision-agriculture acquisition (CapstanAG).
Operating profit grew faster than gross profit because SG&A expenses were roughly flat year-over-year while gross profit rose 8.1%, producing operating leverage.
All three segments grew EBITDA: Industrial Precision Solutions +9%, Medical and Fluid Solutions +3%, Advanced Technology Solutions +22%, the last driven by electronics dispense systems demand.

Q2 earnings included a one-time, non-cash settlement charge to annuitize about 30% of the U.S. pension obligation and a non-cash loss on minority investments, which the company excludes from adjusted results.

Excluding the pension settlement charge, minority-investment loss, and acquisition-related amortization/costs, adjusted EPS rose 18% y/y to a second-quarter record, reflecting underlying operating growth.

Backlog was up 18% y/y with broad-based order entry across all segments; management cited this momentum, plus continued free-cash-flow conversion, as the basis for raising full-year sales and adjusted-EPS guidance.
